title: Structured interviews, and the questions that predict nothing

videos.script: Four people at Caju will interview each finalist for the new role. {{title}} Left to themselves, each would ask what occurred to them, and come away with an impression. Four impressions, overlapping. {{impressions}} Renata gives them something else. The same questions for every candidate, drawn from the job. A scale written before the first interview. And a rule. Score alone, before anybody talks. {{structure}} This lesson is about why. The research puts structured interviews among the best predictors there are. And unstructured ones well below. {{research}} It is about the questions to remove. Puzzles, rituals, trivia, and the ones nobody has the right to ask. {{remove}} And it ends with one question, and the scale that goes with it. {{scale}}
